question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Cranberry juice has a pH value of approximately 3.4.
- Grapefruit juice has a pH value of approximately 4.0.
- Substances with pH values below 7 are acidic.

The student wants to say what cranberry juice and grapefruit juice have in common. Which choice best uses information from the notes to do this?
a: Cranberry juice and grapefruit juice are both acidic substances.
b: Cranberry juice has a pH value that makes it acidic.
c: Cranberry juice and grapefruit juice have pH values of approximately 3.4.
d: Some acidic substances have pH values of approximately 4.0.

question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In a 2021 study, researchers showed participants sets of images.
- Each set contained an unaltered image of a different character or logo alongside two slightly altered versions.
- Participants were asked to identify the correct version in each set.
- In the set containing Pikachu, 26.8% of participants selected the correct version, and 73.2% selected an altered version.
- In the set containing Scooby-Doo, 80.6% of participants identified the correct version, and 19.4% selected an altered version.

The student wants to explain how participants performed on the set with Scooby-Doo. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
a: Pikachu and Scooby-Doo were both included in a 2021 study.
b: When shown an image set of Scooby-Doo, 80.6% of participants identified the correct version, and 19.4% selected an altered version.
c: In a 2021 study, researchers showed participants sets of images containing unaltered versions of popular characters or logos, such as Scooby-Doo, alongside two altered versions.
d: While 80.6% of participants selected the correct version of Scooby-Doo, just 26.8% selected the correct version Pikachu.
